title: bash-classify sensitive paths
description: Paths that hold a credential. A token naming one of these floors the risk of the expression at HIGH. The file bundled with the package is extended by $BASH_CLASSIFY_CONFIG_DIR/sensitive-paths.yaml or ~/.config/bash-classify/sensitive-paths.yaml; a user rule that reuses a bundled name replaces that rule.

name.description: Rule name, unique within the file; reported back on every hit

paths.description: Spellings of the same secret; a token that matches any of them hits the rule

except_paths.description: Specific files exempted from this rule, such as a committed .env.example. Matched the same way as paths, except that a glob in the token is not honored, so a token cannot exempt itself by writing .e*

Path.description: Slash-separated path segments that must appear in the token, in order and next to each other. Never anchored, so a leading slash is decoration. A segment may carry a glob (*, ?, [...]) for a part that varies, such as /proc/*/environ
